The idea

Made for the
occasion.

A celebration is made of many little moments. The welcome, the first plate, the second helping. This identity brings a confident, generous character to professional catering.

The original ornamental mark, playful wordmark and vivid red are the foundation. This expanded study connects them across event imagery, guest-facing print, takeaway packaging and food campaigns.

Design
Eyilade Oridamisi
Scope
Identity, art direction, guest details, packaging & campaign concepts
Context
Portfolio concept development. New people, event scenes and mockups are AI-assisted visualisations with fictional models.

Owambes selected · Manual browsing

The original identity

A flourish with
real presence.

The ornamental symbol feels at home at a celebration. Charcoal grounds the playful lettering; vivid red gives the identity its appetite.

One mark, many touchpoints

A detail that
brings it together.

The supplied rosette moves from a large brand moment to a menu edge, a napkin band or a small closure seal.

The service story

Before the first plate.
Behind every occasion.

The art direction makes room for the work around the meal: preparation, presentation and the human exchange at the table.

At the guest’s place

Set the table.
Set the tone.

A red block gives the menu a confident face. White space keeps the food choices clear, and a small rosette carries the identity onto the napkin.

An appetite for colour

A little closer
to the flavour.

Food textures do the talking: a rich curry, rice and roasted chicken, a crisp golden bite. These visual directions build on the food imagery in the original project.

From the table, with you

One more
brand moment.

A broad red band, a white carrier and a small seal bring the same visual language to take-home packaging. Simple surfaces keep the original mark recognisable.

Room for something smaller

Big occasions.
Closer gatherings.

The same hospitality can feel at home around a smaller table. A quieter part of the story keeps space for family and familiar faces.

Pass a plate.
Share a moment.
Stay a little.

A complete campaign language

From the room
to the screen.

A bold original signature, real-looking gestures and a direct supporting voice. The event story carries across larger compositions and smaller digital formats.

Where it began

The original
foundation.

The original brand guide set the mark, palette and typographic character. The expanded study builds around that foundation, giving the identity more ways to appear in the world.

New scenes depict fictional people and events. Food names are descriptive concept copy. They do not establish an approved menu or claim actual customers, staff or venues.
